paper.title_en: Strong-field dynamics and QPO constraints of charged dilatonic black holes in dilaton-massive gravity
paper.abstract_en: We investigate the strong-field phenomenology of a charged dilatonic black hole in dilaton-massive gravity, focusing on its horizon structure, test-particle dynamics, circular-orbit stability, quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs), observational parameter constraints, and particle-collision energetics. We first analyze the event horizon and show that, within the parameter ranges considered, variations of these parameters can substantially shift the horizon radius. The dynamics of neutral test particles are then studied through the Hamiltonian and effective-potential formalisms. The effective potential, specific energy, specific angular momentum, effective radial force, and innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) exhibit pronounced parameter-dependent modifications in the strong-field region. In particular, the ISCO analysis demonstrates that the additional electromagnetic and massive-gravity contributions shift the boundary separating stable and unstable circular motion, while numerical trajectories reveal corresponding changes in orbital morphology and precessional behavior relative to the Schwarzschild reference case. We further investigate high-frequency twin-peak QPOs within the relativistic precession model by identifying the upper frequency with the azimuthal orbital frequency and the lower frequency with the periastron-precession frequency. The predicted frequencies display measurable sensitivity to <math altimg="si64.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1443"><mi>Q</mi></math>, <math altimg="si65.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1448"><msub><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub></math>, <math altimg="si66.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1458"><msub><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math>, and <math altimg="si67.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1469"><msub><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math>, establishing a direct connection between modifications of the spacetime geometry and characteristic strong-field timing observables. Bayesian parameter estimation is subsequently performed using Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampling and the twin-peak QPO measurements of GRS 1915+105 and H1743–322. Finally, the center-of-mass energy of colliding neutral particles is examined, revealing enhanced sensitivity to the modified geometry in the near-black-hole region and progressively weaker parameter dependence at larger radii. •Charged dilatonic black holes show strong parameter-dependent orbital dynamics.•Electric charge and graviton mass strongly shift the horizon and ISCO radii.•QPO frequencies probe the effects of charge and massive-gravity couplings.•MCMC fits constrain model parameters using GRS 1915+105 and H1743–322.•Particle collisions gain higher center-of-mass energy near the black hole.
